title: Top reviewers
context: Customer Trust wants to celebrate the most active reviewers.
task: For each customer with 3 or more reviews, return first_name, last_name and review_count.
hint: JOIN then GROUP BY, HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3.
answer: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(*) AS review_count FROM reviews r JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;

title: Countries with 3+ customers
context: Localisation only invests where there's a customer base.
task: Return country and customer_count for countries with more than 2 customers.
hint: HAVING COUNT(*) > 2.
answer: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country HAVING COUNT(*) > 2;

title: Revenue per category
context: Finance is closing the quarter and needs revenue by product category.
task: Return category and revenue = SUM(quantity * unit_price) from order_items joined to products, only for delivered orders, rounded to 2 decimals.
hint: Join order_items → products and order_items → orders; filter status.
answer: SELECT p.category, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY p.category;

title: Units sold per product
context: Supply planning needs demand per SKU.
task: Return name and units_sold = total quantity across all order items, for every product that has been ordered.
hint: SUM(quantity) GROUP BY product.
answer: SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id;

title: Spend per customer
context: The loyalty team ranks customers by lifetime value.
task: Return first_name, last_name and total_spend = sum of total_amount over delivered orders, for customers with at least one delivered order.
hint: Filter status in WHERE before grouping.
answer: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, ROUND(SUM(o.total_amount), 2) AS total_spend FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY c.customer_id;

title: Customers who never ordered
context: Re-engagement email targets signups with zero orders.
task: Return first_name, last_name and email for customers with no rows in orders.
hint: LEFT JOIN orders and keep rows where order_id IS NULL.
answer: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, c.email FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;

title: Headcount per warehouse, including empty
context: Ops wants to see every site, even ones with nobody assigned.
task: Return warehouse_name and headcount for every warehouse (0 where no employees).
hint: LEFT JOIN from warehouses; COUNT(e.employee_id).
answer: SELECT w.warehouse_name, COUNT(e.employee_id) AS headcount FROM warehouses w LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id;

title: Products never reviewed
context: The reviews team seeds feedback for silent products.
task: Return name for products that have no reviews.
hint: LEFT JOIN reviews, filter review_id IS NULL.
answer: SELECT p.name FROM products p LEFT JOIN reviews r ON r.product_id = p.product_id WHERE r.review_id IS NULL;

title: Above-average priced products
context: Pricing flags items priced above the catalogue average.
task: Return name and price for products priced above the average price of all products.
hint: Scalar subquery in WHERE.
answer: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products);

title: Customers who bought Electronics
context: The devices team wants its buyer list.
task: Return distinct first_name and last_name of customers who have ordered at least one product in the 'Electronics' category.
hint: customer_id IN (subquery through orders → order_items → products).
answer: SELECT DISTINCT c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c WHERE c.customer_id IN (SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics');

title: Highest-paid per department
context: HR wants the top earner in each department.
task: Return first_name, last_name, department and salary for employees earning the maximum salary within their department.
hint: Correlated subquery: salary = (SELECT MAX(salary) ... WHERE department = e.department).
answer: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, e.department, e.salary FROM employees e WHERE e.salary = (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE department = e.department);

title: Products with a 5-star review
context: Marketing wants to badge top-rated items.
task: Return name for products that have at least one review with rating = 5.
hint: WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reviews ...).
answer: SELECT p.name FROM products p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reviews r WHERE r.product_id = p.product_id AND r.rating = 5);

title: Prime members with no reviews
context: Prime members are prompted to review after delivery.
task: Return first_name and last_name of Prime members who have never written a review.
hint: NOT EXISTS.
answer: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c WHERE c.prime_member = 1 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reviews r WHERE r.customer_id = c.customer_id);

title: Price tiers
context: The filter sidebar buckets products by price.
task: Return name and tier: 'Premium' if price >= 150, 'Standard' if price >= 40, else 'Budget'.
hint: CASE WHEN ordered from highest to lowest.
answer: SELECT name, CASE WHEN price >= 150 THEN 'Premium' WHEN price >= 40 THEN 'Standard' ELSE 'Budget' END AS tier FROM products;

title: Prime vs non-Prime revenue
context: Finance wants a one-row split of delivered revenue.
task: Return prime_revenue and non_prime_revenue as sums of delivered total_amount, using conditional aggregation, rounded to 2 decimals.
hint: SUM(CASE WHEN c.prime_member = 1 THEN total_amount ELSE 0 END).
answer: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN c.prime_member = 1 THEN o.total_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS prime_revenue, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN c.prime_member = 0 THEN o.total_amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS non_prime_revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered';

title: Order status pivot per country
context: The ops dashboard shows a status breakdown by country.
task: Return country, delivered, cancelled and returned counts per country (orders joined to customers).
hint: COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'delivered' THEN 1 END).
answer: SELECT c.country, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'delivered' THEN 1 END) AS delivered, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) AS cancelled, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'returned' THEN 1 END) AS returned FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.country;

title: Orders per month
context: The revenue chart needs monthly buckets.
task: Return month (formatted YYYY-MM) and order_count for each month, sorted by month.
hint: strftime('%Y-%m', order_date).
answer: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;

title: Monthly delivered revenue
context: Finance tracks recognised revenue by month.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM) and revenue (sum of total_amount, 2 decimals) for delivered orders, sorted by month.
hint: Filter status, group by strftime.
answer: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, ROUND(SUM(total_amount), 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;

title: Signup cohort sizes
context: Growth tracks how many customers joined each year.
task: Return signup_year (as integer) and customers count per year.
hint: CAST(strftime('%Y', signup_date) AS INTEGER).
answer: SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', signup_date) AS INTEGER) AS signup_year, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers GROUP BY signup_year;

title: Days since signup at first order
context: Activation time is a key onboarding metric.
task: For each customer with orders, return first_name and days_to_first_order = julianday(MIN(order_date)) - julianday(signup_date), as an integer.
hint: julianday() difference, wrapped in CAST(... AS INTEGER).
answer: SELECT c.first_name, CAST(julianday(MIN(o.order_date)) - julianday(c.signup_date) AS INTEGER) AS days_to_first_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id;

title: Colleagues in the same warehouse
context: Team pages list who works with whom.
task: Return pairs of employees (a_first, b_first) who share a warehouse, where a's employee_id < b's, to avoid duplicates.
hint: Join employees to itself on warehouse_id with an id inequality.
answer: SELECT a.first_name AS a_first, b.first_name AS b_first FROM employees a JOIN employees b ON a.warehouse_id = b.warehouse_id AND a.employee_id < b.employee_id;

title: Order detail lines
context: The packing slip lists every item with customer name.
task: For order 5001, return the customer's first_name, product name and quantity for each line.
hint: orders → customers, orders → order_items → products.
answer: SELECT c.first_name, p.name, oi.quantity FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE o.order_id = 5001;

title: Average rating per category
context: Category managers are judged on customer satisfaction.
task: Return category and avg_rating (2 decimals) using reviews joined to products.
hint: AVG(rating) GROUP BY category.
answer: SELECT p.category, ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS avg_rating FROM reviews r JOIN products p ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

title: All people in the system
context: A single contact list mixing customers and employees.
task: Return one column person_name (first_name || ' ' || last_name) with every customer and every employee, no duplicates.
hint: UNION removes duplicates; UNION ALL keeps them.
answer: SELECT first_name || ' ' || last_name AS person_name FROM customers UNION SELECT first_name || ' ' || last_name FROM employees;

title: Reviewers who never bought
context: Trust & Safety checks reviews from non-buyers.
task: Return customer_id values that appear in reviews but not in orders.
hint: EXCEPT.
answer: SELECT customer_id FROM reviews EXCEPT SELECT customer_id FROM orders;

title: Customers above average order count
context: Power users get early access to features.
task: Return customer_id and order_count for customers whose order count exceeds the average order count per customer.
hint: Derived table of counts, compare to AVG of that derived table.
answer: SELECT customer_id, order_count FROM (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) t WHERE order_count > (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id));

title: Category share of units
context: A pie chart needs each category's share of units sold.
task: Using a CTE, return category and share_pct = units in that category / total units * 100, rounded to 1 decimal.
hint: WITH totals AS (...) then divide; multiply by 100.0 to avoid integer division.
answer: WITH cat AS (SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category) SELECT category, ROUND(units * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(units) FROM cat), 1) AS share_pct FROM cat;

title: Return rate per country
context: Returns are expensive; where are they coming from?
task: Return country and return_rate_pct = returned orders / total orders * 100, rounded to 1 decimal, for each country with orders.
hint: Conditional COUNT divided by COUNT(*), times 100.0.
answer: WITH t AS (SELECT c.country, COUNT(*) AS total, SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'returned' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS returned FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.country) SELECT country, ROUND(returned * 100.0 / total, 1) AS return_rate_pct FROM t;

title: Warehouses over 30k capacity with staff
context: Capacity planning looks at big sites and their teams.
task: Return warehouse_name, capacity and staff count for warehouses with capacity > 30000 and at least 2 employees.
hint: WHERE on capacity, HAVING on the count.
answer: SELECT w.warehouse_name, w.capacity, COUNT(e.employee_id) AS staff FROM warehouses w JOIN employees e ON e.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id WHERE w.capacity > 30000 GROUP BY w.warehouse_id HAVING COUNT(e.employee_id) >= 2;

title: Products ordered by 5+ distinct customers
context: Merch identifies broadly popular SKUs.
task: Return name and buyer_count = distinct customers who ordered the product, for products with 5 or more distinct buyers.
hint: COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) with HAVING.
answer: SELECT p.name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS buyer_count FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) >= 5;

title: Contactable customers
context: The mailer needs a value in every row.
task: Return first_name and contact = email, or 'no-email' when NULL.
hint: COALESCE(email, 'no-email').
answer: SELECT first_name, COALESCE(email, 'no-email') AS contact FROM customers;

title: Email domains
context: Marketing analyses which email providers customers use.
task: Return domain (text after '@') and customer_count for customers with an email, grouped by domain.
hint: SUBSTR(email, INSTR(email, '@') + 1).
answer: SELECT SUBSTR(email, INSTR(email, '@') + 1) AS domain, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers WHERE email IS NOT NULL GROUP BY domain;

title: Orders with mismatched totals
context: An audit checks that order totals equal the sum of their lines.
task: Return order_id, total_amount and item_sum = SUM(quantity * unit_price) for orders where the two differ by more than 0.01.
hint: Group items by order, compare with ABS().
answer: SELECT o.order_id, o.total_amount, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS item_sum FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id HAVING ABS(o.total_amount - SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price)) > 0.01;
